801 Solving Trigonometric Equations using the ASTC Method

examples.question_text: Simplify $3\cot\theta-3\cot\theta\cos^{2}\theta$ in terms of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$, wherever it is defined.

examples.solution_text: $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(\sin x-\cos x)^{2}+2\sin x\cos x\\&=\sin^{2}x-2\sin x\cos x+\cos^{2}x+2\sin x\cos x\\&=\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x\\&=1\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Show that $\frac{5\cos^{2}\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{5\cos^{2}\theta}{1-\sin\theta}$ is independent of $\theta$ wherever it is defined.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5\cos^{2}\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{5\cos^{2}\theta}{1-\sin\theta}\\&=5\cos^{2}\theta\frac{(1-\sin\theta)+(1+\sin\theta)}{(1+\sin\theta)(1-\sin\theta)}\\&=5\cos^{2}\theta\frac{2}{1-\sin^{2}\theta}\\&=5\cos^{2}\theta\frac{2}{\cos^{2}\theta}\\&=10\end{aligned}$

The constant result is independent of $\theta$ on the original domain, where $\cos\theta\ne0$.

examples.derivation: Using secθ = 1/cosθ and cotθ = cosθ/sinθ, the product becomes 2/sinθ = 2cosecθ on its original domain.
Since cosec²x − cot²x = 1, factoring out 3 gives 3.
Factorisation gives 3cotθ(1 − cos²θ) = 3cotθ sin²θ. Substituting cotθ = cosθ/sinθ gives 3sinθ cosθ.
The squared quotient products reduce to 5sin²α and 5cos²α. Their sum is 5(sin²α + cos²α) = 5.
Expansion gives sin²x − 2sinx cosx + cos²x + 2sinx cosx. The mixed terms cancel, leaving sin²x + cos²x = 1.
Difference-of-squares factorisation gives 2(sec²x − tan²x)(sec²x + tan²x) − 4tan²x. Using sec²x − tan²x = 1 leaves 2(sec²x − tan²x) = 2.
Combining the fractions gives 5cos²θ × 2/(1 − sin²θ) = 10. Both original denominators are nonzero exactly when cosθ is nonzero, so cancellation and the domain statement are valid.
The numerator becomes 2(sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sinθ cosθ) = 2/(sinθ cosθ). The denominator is 1/(sinθ cosθ), giving 2 wherever the original expression is defined.
